blocks.source: Vol III, Tool Calling, § Designing the Active Toolkit
blocks.md: Across the `src/pool.py` repair, the agent has needed to inspect source files, apply candidate patches, run test suites, and read diagnostics, and how the runtime packages those capabilities into a toolkit can fail at either extreme. If each tool exposes too little functionality per invocation, the model must coordinate low-level state across dozens of turns.

questions.q: The section **Designing the Active Toolkit** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A program that acts with its own legitimate authority on behalf of a less privileged requester can be steered to misuse that authority, so authority must follow the request, not the program.

A logical operation ID names one intended effect across attempts, each attempt gets a fresh attempt ID, and the ID is safe only under an endpoint contract that binds it to caller, scope, and arguments.
A click keeps every tool-boundary invariant while losing atomicity, so each observation carries capture, window, and coordinate mapping and target identity is rechecked before dispatch.
A mutating tool over an endpoint without deduplication ships actuate, probe, and compensate together, with the probe written before dispatch against a captured baseline.
